g.passage: I had lent Errol eleven rupees in the spring, and he had promised to repay me by the monsoon, when he would surely be restored to the side. Each excuse asked for another week. I granted them, believing a week a small thing to give a young man. Only when the rains came, and Shirin told me he had taken work hauling ice on the night boats, did I understand that every week I had lent him was a week he had spent elsewhere, and that the money had never been the larger debt. g.explanation: 화자는 아들이 대학으로 떠나는 상황에서 씨앗을 고르며 자라날 것은 남기고 나머지는 흘려보낸다고 말한다. 마지막 부분에서 먼 계절을 위해 병을 봉해 두는 행동도 소중한 것을 지키며 떠나보내는 태도를 보여 준다. 따라서 체는 지킬 것을 붙잡고 나머지를 놓아주는 어머니의 역할을 뜻하므로 C가 맞다. A는 체의 '새는' 성질을 기억력으로, D는 결함으로 오해했고, B는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었다.

seed.conflict: about keeping a family business open
seed.topicSeed: a salt flat in Kyoto; best friends after a move about keeping a family business open

g.passage: Akari had not seen Ivan since he moved to Madrid, so when he appeared at the edge of her family's salt pans on the coast north of Kyoto, she nearly dropped her rake. He wanted to know whether the business was still open. Barely, she admitted. Her father wanted to sell the land to a resort; her aunt wanted to keep raking until the last buyer stopped calling. Ivan walked with her across the white crust, listening, and said little. When she finally asked what he would do, he told her that a business, like a friendship, survives on small deposits. She thought of the letters he had sent every month from Spain, each one short, none of them skipped. That evening they raked the pans together until the light went copper over the bay.
g.question: As used in the text, the phrase “survives on small deposits” most nearly suggests
options: a careful saving of money in case the business must soon close.
the thin layer of salt that remains after the seawater dries.
a willingness to accept small profits instead of selling the land.
steady, modest efforts made consistently over a long time.
g.explanation: Ivan은 사업도 우정처럼 작은 예치금으로 살아남는다고 말한다. 곧이어 Akari는 그가 매달 짧지만 한 번도 거르지 않고 보낸 편지를 떠올린다. 두 부분을 이으면 이 표현은 꾸준하고 작은 노력을 뜻하므로 D가 맞다. A와 C는 '예치금'을 돈으로, B는 소금 퇴적으로 문자 그대로 읽었다.

seed.conflict: over how to mark an anniversary
seed.topicSeed: an apartment stairwell in the Cornish coast; an author and her translator over how to mark an anniversary

g.passage: Anniversaries mattered to Pilar. Ten years after her first novel appeared, she wished to mark the date with a dinner, speeches, and a printed card. Eulalio, who had carried her sentences into English through three books, preferred to say nothing at all. They argued about it on the stairwell of her lodging above the harbor on the Cornish coast, she on the landing, he two steps below, the wind from the sea rattling the skylight. At last he told her that his part of the work had always been a lamp in the next room: it lit her pages, but no one was meant to see it burning. Pilar was silent for a long moment, then asked him to write the card himself. A gull walked the slate roof overhead, its claws scraping at every step.
g.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a lamp in the next room” most nearly suggests
options: a contribution that helps others see while staying unnoticed itself.
a source of warmth that Pilar has failed to share with her translator.
a private habit of working late, long after Pilar has gone to bed.
a feeling of being shut out from the celebrations Pilar has planned.
g.explanation: Eulalio는 세 권의 책을 번역했지만 기념일에 아무 말도 하지 않기를 원한다. 그는 자기 몫이 옆방의 등불처럼 그녀의 글을 비추되 타는 모습은 보이지 않는 것이라고 설명한다. 따라서 이 표현은 드러나지 않으면서 남을 돕는 기여를 뜻하므로 A가 맞다. B, C, D는 각각 냉담, 야근 습관, 소외감으로 읽어 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
